nodes.label: socket.io connection accepted
nodes.detail: Every UI-initiated action passes through here. Right after connecting it returns sendInfo, and emits setup when the instance is not set up yet.

nodes.label: Login-required guard
nodes.detail: Throws "You are not logged in." when socket.userID is missing. The caller's catch answers the callback with ok:false.

nodes.label: Broadcast the monitor list
nodes.detail: Sends the monitor list on monitorList after login. The "Add a monitor" choices in edit mode come from this list.

nodes.label: New page button
nodes.detail: The button on the status page list screen. It only router-navigates to /add-status-page; nothing is sent to the server.

nodes.label: Next button
nodes.detail: Submits the name and the slug. Both are required. Disabled while processing, which prevents a double submit.

nodes.label: Send the creation to the server
nodes.detail: Emits addStatusPage. On success it navigates to /status/<slug>?edit. A UNIQUE constraint is replaced with a dedicated message.

nodes.label: Add a status page
nodes.detail: Trims title/slug. Empty gives "Please input all fields". The slug is lowercased and registered once it passes checkSlug.

nodes.label: Slug format check
nodes.detail: A regex allowing letters, digits and hyphens, with no repeated hyphen. A non-string, an empty value or a mismatch throws Invalid Slug.

nodes.label: Delete button in the list
nodes.detail: Appears on row hover. click.stop.prevent blocks the link navigation and only opens the confirm dialog.

nodes.label: Delete confirm dialog
nodes.detail: A yes/no Confirm. Yes runs deleteStatusPage. No does nothing.

nodes.label: Send the delete from the list
nodes.detail: Emits deleteStatusPage. After the success toast it calls window.location.reload() to refetch the list.

nodes.label: List receive handler
nodes.detail: Takes the list from the statusPageList event and sets statusPageListLoaded to true. A spinner shows until it arrives.

nodes.label: Send the list to the client
nodes.detail: Fetches every status_page ordered by title, runs toJSON and emits statusPageList. Called exactly once, right after login.

nodes.label: Public status page
nodes.detail: What visitors see. It renders nothing until loadedTheme is set. The editing sidebar exists only while enableEditMode is on.

nodes.label: Visitor's browser
nodes.detail: GETs /status/<slug>. No login needed, anyone can read it. A 5-minute apicache applies.

nodes.label: GET /status/:slug
nodes.detail: Lowercases the slug and renders server-side. apicache 5 minutes. /status and /status-page fall back to slug=default.

nodes.label: GET / entry routing
nodes.detail: If the host name is in the custom domain table, that page is rendered server-side. If entryPage starts with statusPage-, it goes to /status/…, otherwise /dashboard.

nodes.label: Return the public page
nodes.detail: A slug of index.html is read as default. No match returns 404 with the bare indexHTML (the Vue side then shows page-not-found).

nodes.label: Assemble the HTML
nodes.detail: Uses cheerio to swap in the title, description, OG tags and favicon, and embeds preloadData into a script tag.

nodes.label: Fetch all page data
nodes.detail: Collects the public config, the pinned incidents (pin=1 AND active=1), the public groups and the active maintenance windows in one pass.

nodes.label: Narrow to the public settings
nodes.detail: Returns only slug / title / description / theme / CSS and the like. domainNameList is excluded — this is not the same as the admin toJSON.

nodes.label: Group in public form
nodes.detail: Shapes the monitors under the group in weight order. showTags and the certificate expiry flag change which fields come back.

nodes.label: Fetch the active maintenance
nodes.detail: Of the linked maintenance windows, returns only the ones where isUnderMaintenance is true. An exception is swallowed and an empty array returned.

nodes.label: Screen init
nodes.detail: Decide the slug, getData, arm the auto-refresh timer, then run updateHeartbeatList and loadIncidentHistory. With ?edit it starts in edit mode.

nodes.label: Fetch the settings data
nodes.detail: If window.preloadData exists it resolves immediately with no request. Otherwise it GETs /api/status-page/<slug>. A 404 goes to /page-not-found.

nodes.label: GET settings API
nodes.detail: /api/status-page/:slug. No match calls sendHttpError. The 5-minute apicache means a stale value can come back right after a save.

nodes.label: GET manifest.json
nodes.detail: For the PWA. Returns only the name and the icons. apicache is 1440 minutes = 24 hours, so a logo change takes a long time to appear.

nodes.label: GET status badge SVG
nodes.detail: Works out Up/Degraded/Down/Maintenance from the latest beat of the public monitors and returns an SVG. With no monitors it is N/A (grey).

nodes.label: External analytics
nodes.detail: Only google / umami / plausible / matomo / rybbit are allowed. The script is injected into head only when the settings are valid.

nodes.label: Auto-refresh the heartbeat data
nodes.detail: Does not run in edit mode (the websocket side is used there). After fetching it updates the down-count badge on the favicon and the countdown to the next refresh.

nodes.label: GET heartbeat API
nodes.detail: Returns the last 100 beats and the 24-hour uptime for every monitor under the public groups. apicache 1 minute.

nodes.label: Slug to ID
nodes.detail: SELECT id FROM status_page WHERE slug=?. On a miss it is undefined and the caller answers "slug is not found".

nodes.label: Edit page button
nodes.detail: Shown only when signed in (hasToken). Pressing it opens the sidebar and switches the rendering from viewing to editing.

nodes.label: Enter edit mode
nodes.detail: Opens an authenticated connection with initSocketIO(true) and sets enableEditMode to true. Without a socket connection, editMode stays false.

nodes.label: Fetch the admin settings
nodes.detail: Login required. Fetches one row by slug and returns toJSON. Nothing found gives "No slug?". This is the only path that includes the domain list.

nodes.label: Shape for the admin view
nodes.detail: On top of the public fields it carries id, published and domainNameList. domainNameList is looked up backwards from the in-memory domain table.

nodes.label: Custom domain list
nodes.detail: Walks the static domainMappingList rather than the DB and returns only the entries matching its own slug. It was loaded at startup.

nodes.label: Add group button
nodes.detail: Edit mode only. Pressing it just appends to a local array; nothing reaches the DB until you save.

nodes.label: Add a group at the top
nodes.detail: The first one is "Services", every later one is "Untitled Group". It uses unshift, so the newest group lands on top.

nodes.label: Monitor picker
nodes.detail: Only monitors not already published are offered. Choosing one creates a group if there is none and adds it to the first group.

nodes.label: Replace the logo image
nodes.detail: Clicking the logo opens the crop dialog. It does not open outside edit mode. The x resets it to /icon.svg.

nodes.label: Hold the cropped result
nodes.detail: It only puts the data:image/png string into imgDataUrl. Turning it into a real file happens on the server at save time.

nodes.label: Add domain button
nodes.detail: The + in the sidebar. It just adds one empty input row. Left empty, it is skipped by the save.

nodes.label: Remove domain button
nodes.detail: The x splices that row out of the array. The DB only catches up at save time, through a delete-all-then-recreate.

nodes.label: Save button
nodes.detail: At the bottom of the sidebar. Disabled while loading. A successful save navigates to the new slug's URL and closes edit mode.

nodes.label: Discard button
nodes.detail: Reloads /status/<original slug> with no confirmation. Every unsaved change is lost.

nodes.label: Send the saved content
nodes.detail: Trims and lowercases the slug and emits saveStatusPage. On success it waits up to 100 ms and then navigates to the new URL.

nodes.label: Save the status page
nodes.detail: Login required. Saves the settings, the logo, the domains and the public groups in one go. published and password are left untouched.

nodes.label: Save the logo as PNG
nodes.detail: Only a data: URL of type image/png is allowed; anything else gives "Only allowed PNG logo." It is written to upload as logo<id>.png.

nodes.label: Update the custom domains
nodes.detail: In a transaction it deletes all of its own rows and re-registers them. If another page has the same domain, it takes it over. A non-array throws.

nodes.label: Reload the domain table
nodes.detail: Loads the domain-to-slug table from the DB into memory. Called at startup and right after a save; it drives the entry URL routing.

nodes.label: Drop the HTTP cache
nodes.detail: Clears the entire cache right after a save or a delete. Without it, the stale public page is served for five minutes.

nodes.label: Update the entry page setting
nodes.detail: Only when entryPage points at this page: it follows a slug change, and on delete it goes back to dashboard.

nodes.label: Delete in the danger zone
nodes.detail: At the very bottom of the edit sidebar. Pressing it opens a confirm dialog. Nothing is deleted here.

nodes.label: Delete confirm dialog
nodes.detail: Yes runs deleteStatusPage. On success it returns to /manage-status-page.

nodes.label: Send the delete to the server
nodes.detail: Emits deleteStatusPage. On success it leaves edit mode and goes to the list. A failure only shows an error toast and the screen stays.

nodes.label: Delete the status page
nodes.detail: Login required. Manually DELETEs incidents, then groups, then the page itself. cname rows go through the foreign key cascade.

nodes.label: Create an incident
nodes.detail: Edit mode only. Pressing it opens an empty post form above the content. Any existing draft is set aside.

nodes.label: Open the post form
nodes.detail: Creates an empty incident with style defaulting to primary. Anything being edited is parked in previousIncident.

nodes.label: Style picker
nodes.detail: Six choices: info / warning / danger / primary / light / dark. Choosing one changes the box's background class immediately.

nodes.label: Post button
nodes.detail: The title and the body are contenteditable. Pressing it emits post to the parent. Markdown works.

nodes.label: Cancel button
nodes.detail: Closes the form and restores the previous draft if one was parked. Nothing is sent to the server.

nodes.label: Send the post
nodes.detail: An empty title or body stops it with a toast. On success it closes the form and reloads the history.

nodes.label: Cancel editing the post
nodes.detail: Sets enableEditIncidentMode back to false and, if previousIncident exists, restores the original content.

nodes.label: Post an incident
nodes.detail: Login required. Saved with pin=1 and active=1. With an id it updates and stamps the updated time; without one it creates and stamps the created time.

nodes.label: Resolve button
nodes.detail: Appears on a pinned card in edit mode. Pressing it goes straight to the server — there is no confirm dialog.

nodes.label: Send the resolve to the server
nodes.detail: Emits resolveIncident and toasts the result. On success it reloads the history and the card leaves the pinned area.

nodes.label: Resolve an incident
nodes.detail: Login required. Identifies the row by both slug and id. No match answers "Incident not found or access denied".

nodes.label: Mark it resolved
nodes.detail: Sets active=false and pin=false and stamps the updated time. It is not deleted — it stays in the past incidents list.

nodes.label: Unpin every post at once
nodes.detail: Login required. Sets every pin=1 on that page to 0. active is left alone. Nothing in the current UI reaches it.

nodes.label: Unpin method
nodes.detail: A method that emits unpinIncident, but no button in the template calls it — dead code.

nodes.label: Edit button on a pinned post
nodes.detail: Edit on the pinned card. It switches to an inline edit form in place rather than a modal.

nodes.label: Start inline editing
nodes.detail: Copies the target into the edit slot. Saving goes through postIncident, so pin and active go back to true.

nodes.label: Edit button in the history
nodes.detail: The pencil in the past incidents list. Edit mode only. It opens IncidentManageModal.

nodes.label: Save in the modal
nodes.detail: Edits the title, body, style and pinned flag. While processing it shows a spinner and cannot be pressed.

nodes.label: Send the edit
nodes.detail: Empty fields are rejected on the client too. On success it closes the modal, tells the parent with incident-updated and reloads the history.

nodes.label: Edit an incident
nodes.detail: Login required. validateIncident rejects empty fields. An invalid style is forced to warning before saving.

nodes.label: Validate the post
nodes.detail: Throws when the title or the body is only whitespace. Only editIncident uses it; postIncident never does.

nodes.label: Delete button on a pinned post
nodes.detail: Delete on the pinned card. Pressing it opens the confirm dialog inside the modal. It is not an immediate delete.

nodes.label: Delete button in the history
nodes.detail: The trash can in the past incidents list. Edit mode only. It leads to the confirm dialog.

nodes.label: Delete confirm dialog
nodes.detail: A yes/no Confirm. Yes sends deleteIncident. No drops the target and does nothing.

nodes.label: Send the delete to the server
nodes.detail: Does nothing when there is no pending target. It toasts the result and, on success, tells the parent and reloads the history.

nodes.label: Delete an incident
nodes.detail: Login required. Hard-deletes exactly one row matching both slug and id. No match returns not found.

nodes.label: Resolve button in the history
nodes.detail: Shown only while it is unresolved (active). Pressing it runs resolveIncident at once. There is no confirmation.

nodes.label: Load more button
nodes.detail: Shown only while hasMore is true. Disabled with a spinner while loading. Each press adds ten more.

nodes.label: Load the next page
nodes.detail: Runs only while hasMore and nextCursor are both set. Fetches with the cursor and appends to the existing list.

nodes.label: Fetch the history
nodes.detail: In edit mode it goes over the socket; for a visitor it goes over HTTP. The HTTP path shows no toast when it fails.

nodes.label: Fetch the history (socket)
nodes.detail: No login required. It decides isPublic from whether userID is set and passes it on, but the receiving side never uses the value.

nodes.label: GET history API
nodes.detail: Fetches the next page with the cursor query. apicache 5 minutes. A missing page returns Status Page Not Found.

nodes.label: Fetch the history by page
nodes.detail: Ten at a time, created_date descending. The cursor is the last created time. Resolved and unresolved are returned alike.

nodes.label: Shape the post for the public
nodes.detail: Returns id, style, title, body, pin, active and the created/updated times. The body is rendered as Markdown and sanitized on the client.

nodes.label: RSS reader
nodes.detail: An outside subscriber that polls /status/<slug>/rss. No authentication — anyone can subscribe.

nodes.label: GET RSS feed
nodes.detail: apicache 5 minutes. A missing page returns 404 with the bare indexHTML (note: not RSS).

nodes.label: Build the RSS response
nodes.detail: Looks the page up by slug, builds the feed URL and returns it as application/rss+xml.

nodes.label: Decide the feed URL
nodes.detail: x-forwarded-proto/host are honoured only while trustProxy is on. With no request it is built from the config.

nodes.label: Assemble the RSS XML
nodes.detail: The title is rss_title first, then the page title. Pinned incidents and monitors that are down become the items.

nodes.label: Collect the RSS data
nodes.detail: Pulls the latest beat for each monitor and works out the overall status. Only the DOWN ones stay in the feed.

nodes.label: Work out the overall status
nodes.detail: Any maintenance means maintenance. No UP at all means everything is down; a mix means partially degraded. Zero monitors gives -1.

nodes.label: DNS for the custom domain
nodes.detail: The user has to point a CNAME at Uptime Kuma. The app only matches on the Host name.

nodes.label: status_page
nodes.detail: slug is UNIQUE. The published / search_engine_index / password columns exist, but the save never writes them, so they keep their defaults.

nodes.label: status_page_cname
nodes.detail: Maps custom domains to pages. domain is UNIQUE. Rows go away in the cascade when the status_page is deleted.

nodes.label: incident
nodes.detail: pin and active default to true. status_page_id has no foreign key, so deleting a page needs a manual DELETE.

nodes.label: group
nodes.detail: The public groups. Narrowed by public=1 and status_page_id. Anything not in the submitted list is deleted during a save.

nodes.label: monitor_group
nodes.detail: Maps groups to monitors. Every save deletes and recreates it per group, and weight is renumbered.

nodes.label: monitor
nodes.detail: The monitors shown on the public page. The names and tags come from here.

nodes.label: heartbeat
nodes.detail: The check results. The public page reads the last 100, while the badge and the RSS read only the latest one, by time descending.

nodes.label: setting
nodes.detail: Holds entryPage, trustProxy and more. If a status page is the entry point, this is updated too.

nodes.label: maintenance
nodes.detail: Scheduled maintenance. Only the windows currently running appear on the public page.

nodes.label: maintenance_status_page
nodes.detail: Maps maintenance windows to status pages. Only windows linked here show up on the public page.

flows.title: Create a status page
flows.trigger: "New Status Page" on the status page list, then a name and a slug and "Next"

steps.label: The name or the slug is empty

notes: It goes straight into edit mode after creation (mounted sees the trailing ?edit in the URL and calls edit())
A duplicate slug is detected only by looking for the string "UNIQUE constraint" in the DB error, so a different database engine would lose the dedicated message
At creation there are no groups and no monitors. Until you save, the public page reads "nothing here"

flows.title: Open a status page in edit mode
flows.trigger: The "Edit Status Page" button at the top of the public page (shown only while signed in)

steps.label: Shape it for the admin view
Create a group if there is none

notes: editMode is true only when both enableEditMode and the socket connection are. While disconnected, pressing the button does not switch the rendering to editing
In edit mode the auto-refresh (HTTP polling) stops and the heartbeat data switches to the websocket values
Adding a group, a monitor or a domain are all local array operations. Nothing in the DB changes until you press Save
The discard button reloads with no confirmation, so unsaved changes are gone

flows.title: Save the edits
flows.trigger: The "Save" button at the bottom of the edit sidebar

steps.label: Fetch one row by the original slug
Aborted for an invalid analytics type
Roll back on an invalid value
Delete the groups that are no longer listed
Navigate to the new slug's URL

notes: published, search_engine_index and password have columns, but they are commented out in the save, so the UI cannot switch a page between public and private
Monitor membership is DELETEd and re-INSERTed per group every time. The ordering (weight) is renumbered from the on-screen order at save time
The logo accepts only data:image/png. Any other data: URL fails the entire save with "Only allowed PNG logo."
If another page already uses the same domain, it is taken over silently and reassigned to this one
A successful save always navigates to the new slug's URL, so right after changing the slug the old URL 404s
apicache.clear wipes every cache, so other status pages and API responses are thrown away as collateral

flows.title: Delete a status page
flows.trigger: The delete button in the list, or the one in the danger zone at the bottom of the edit sidebar

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Put the entry point back to dashboard

notes: incident and group have no foreign key cascade, so they are DELETEd by hand. Get the order wrong and orphan rows are left behind
monitor_group is never deleted explicitly (nothing in the code guarantees it follows the group delete)
A delete cannot be undone. Every past incident that was posted goes with it
Deleting from the list screen ends with window.location.reload(). Deleting from the edit screen navigates to /manage-status-page

flows.title: A visitor views the public page
flows.trigger: A visitor opens /status/<slug> (or the root of a custom domain)

steps.label: Keep only the ones running now
No preload means an API call

notes: No login needed. The published column is never consulted, so there is effectively no way to make a page private
Server-side rendering embeds window.preloadData, so the first view hits no API. Only a direct client-side render calls /api/status-page/<slug>
apicache holds /status/:slug for 5 minutes and manifest.json for 24 hours. Right after a save the old content can still be served
A slug that does not exist returns 404 with the bare indexHTML, and the front end then redirects to /page-not-found — a two-stage arrangement
getMaintenanceList swallows exceptions and returns an empty array, so maintenance can quietly vanish from the page with nothing to notice

flows.title: The public page refreshes itself
flows.trigger: The auto-refresh timer while the page is open (300 seconds by default, configurable, 5 seconds minimum)

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Return the history and the uptime
A failure does nothing at all

notes: This polling does not run in edit mode (the websocket data is used there)
The interval is max(5, autoRefreshInterval) seconds. Anything under 5 is rounded up to 5
The server-side apicache holds for a minute, so even at a 5-second setting the real data can only change once a minute
setInterval is set twice inside mounted, so two timers run (the earlier ID is overwritten and never cleared)
There is no catch on a failed fetch: nothing appears on screen and lastUpdateTime simply stops advancing

flows.title: Post an incident
flows.trigger: "Create Incident" in edit mode, then writing the body and pressing "Post"

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Show it pinned at the top

notes: postIncident does not validate title/content on the server (only editIncident goes through validateIncident). Whitespace alone can be saved
style is not validated on the server either, so an unexpected string is used directly as a class name
A post is always saved with pin=1 and active=1. Re-editing an existing incident through editIncident puts even a resolved one back on display
The body is Markdown. It is sanitized with DOMPurify before being rendered with v-html
After posting, the history API is called again and the screen is rebuilt. Pinned ones sit at the top, the rest go under "Past Incidents"

flows.title: Resolve an incident
flows.trigger: The "Resolve" button on a pinned card, or the check button in the past incidents list

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Identify one row by slug and id
An id from another page is rejected
It moves to the past list

notes: Resolving is not deleting. It becomes active=0, pin=0 and stays in the "Past Incidents" list
The resolve button has no confirm dialog; it goes to the server the moment it is pressed
Because it matches on both slug and id, an incident ID belonging to another status page is rejected
unpinIncident (unpin everything at once) exists both on the server and as a front-end method, but no button in the template reaches it
The public page's apicache is not explicitly cleared after a resolve, so a visitor can see the old post for up to five minutes

flows.title: Rewrite a posted incident
flows.trigger: The "Edit" button on a pinned card (inline editing), or the pencil button in the past incidents list (modal editing)

steps.label: It reuses the same posting path
Turn the slug into an ID
Identify one row by slug and id
Rejected when there is no match
Save the content and the updated time

notes: There are two ways in and they behave differently. "Edit" on a pinned card uses postIncident, which puts pin and active back to true. The modal uses editIncident, where the pinned flag can be set explicitly
Only the modal path gets the style whitelist check; anything outside it is silently replaced with warning
Modal editing leaves the created time alone and only stamps the updated time, so the order in the past incidents list does not change
editIncident's error responses carry msgi18n:true, yet error.message sometimes holds raw text that is not a translation key

flows.title: Delete an incident
flows.trigger: The "Delete" button on a pinned card, or the trash button in the past incidents list

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Identify one row by slug and id
Rejected when there is no match

notes: The delete is a hard delete and cannot be undone. Unlike resolving, it leaves no history behind
The confirm dialog is the Confirm inside IncidentManageModal, shared by both paths, so deleting from a pinned card shows the same dialog
IncidentManageModal is rendered only while enableEditMode is on, so leaving edit mode takes the delete and edit controls with it

flows.title: Read the past incidents, and load more
flows.trigger: Rendering the "Past Incidents" section of the public page, and pressing "Load more"

steps.label: Turn the slug into an ID
Turn the slug into an ID
Return the rows and the cursor

notes: Ten per page, fixed (INCIDENT_PAGE_SIZE). The cursor is the created_date of the last row, so rows sharing a timestamp can be skipped
The socket version works out isPublic and passes it along, but getIncidentHistory never uses the argument, so a signed-out visitor gets exactly what an admin gets
Nothing filters on resolved or not, so a visitor to the public page can read every past incident
A failure on the HTTP path only reaches the console, with no toast. Only the socket path shows the error on screen
The history API is also cached for 5 minutes, so pressing "Load more" right after posting or resolving can mix in stale content

flows.title: Subscribe to the status by RSS

steps.label: Fetch the posts and the public groups
The latest beat of each monitor

notes: The feed carries only pinned incidents (pin=1 active=1) and monitors that are down right now. Resolved ones never appear
The item ID includes the updated time, so editing an existing incident tends to re-notify subscribers as if it were new
The RSS title is rss_title, then the page title, then a default string. The language is hard-coded to en
For a slug that does not exist it returns 404 with HTML (indexHTML) rather than RSS, which the reader reports as a parse error
apicache holds for 5 minutes, so a new post takes up to five minutes to reach the feed
The latest beat is fetched per monitor with a separate query, so many public monitors make this slow

flows.title: Assign a custom domain
flows.trigger: Adding it to the "Domain Names" field in the edit sidebar, saving, and pointing a DNS CNAME at it

steps.label: Aborted if it is not an array
Delete all of its own rows
Delete the same name on other pages too
No match, forwarded to the entry page

notes: Domain matching only ever consults the in-memory domainMappingList. It is reloaded at startup and on save, so editing the DB directly has no effect
The mapping table is a static variable inside the process. In a multi-process or multi-instance setup, only the process that saved it sees the change
The domain column is UNIQUE. If another status page uses the same domain, it is taken over with no confirmation
Empty rows are skipped at registration, but the row itself stays, so an empty input line is still visible after saving
Only the root of the domain (/) is affected. The /status/<slug> path still works on both, as before
The app does nothing about certificates or the CNAME itself. All it does is match the Host header
